_comment: GENERATED BY MATUGEN - do not edit by hand. Template: ~/.config/matugen/templates/quickshell-colors.json
_policy: Quickshell is the ONE app in this setup that follows Material 3 instead of a fixed Tokyo Night base. Its surfaces come from the wallpaper too, not just its accents. That is safe because M3 roles come in contrast-checked pairs (surface/on_surface, primary/on_primary...) as long as they are used in pairs and never mixed with hardcoded colours. Every other app keeps the fixed-background policy, see the header of config.toml.
_no_error_role: M3 has error/on_error and this file used to emit them, but Theme.qml never read either key -- it declares `warning` and `critical` as hardcoded Tokyo Night literals, because an alert tinted by the wallpaper loses the one thing it is for: over a red image a critical reading would come out the same hue as the rest of the bar. So the two lines wrote a colour nothing could consume. Every other key here is read by a property in Theme.qml; keep it that way, and if some role really is wanted, add the reader in the same change. Same reasoning as the [config] block in config.toml.
